Olivia to run a 24h latency/cost spike benchmark on their top-3 prompts and share results
Bluefield to confirm internal stakeholders for security review by 2026-08-27
Connor to open ticket for the VPC peering setup checklist
action_items: Samir Patel: Share committed pricing spreadsheet and example MSA (due: 2026-08-25)

summary: Quarterly checkpoint covering usage trends (prefix caching & burst), cost anomalies for July, reliability SLOs and upcoming roadmap items. Customer is evaluating a 12-month reserved commitment for Dedicated capacity but needs benchmark data and a security deep-dive before procurement. Agreed to run targeted benchmarks and share committed pricing; follow-ups on VPC peering and SOC2 evidence.
topics: Latency SLOs and KV cache behavior
Roadmap: autoscale policies and canary rollouts
transcript:
Header: 2026-08-21 15:00 UTC | Duration 42m | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Olivia (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood CSM), Rachel (Bluefield Head of ML), Evan (Platform), Priya (SRE), Nina (Procurement)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, sorry for the slight delay, we had a back-to-back. Quick roll call?

[00:12] Rachel: Rachel here.

[00:15] Evan: Evan on platform.

[00:18] Priya: Priya SRE.

[00:20] Nina: Nina procurement.

[00:23] Samir: Cool. Olivia and Diego from our side as well. Intent for today is a short QBR-style checkpoint focused on health: usage, cost, reliability, and next steps on a commitment conversation you flagged.

[01:05] Olivia: I'll share my screen in a sec, but high level first: we looked at your July telemetry — saw an unusual token cost bump around July 12–14 where your average tokens per request spiked and we got a few fallback routes to the larger model which increased spend.

[01:30] Rachel: Yeah that's the period we ran the new triage workflow in staging then flipped to prod, there might have been a prompt template mis-scope.

[01:42] Evan: Confirming, we did a batch migration for the Triage pipe and some of the prompts didn't get the pruning logic.

[01:50] Olivia: That aligns. We also noticed prefix cache hit rates dipped — so KV cash — the auto-prefix/kv cache wasn't warming as expected which made continuous batching less effective.

[02:10] Priya: "KV cash" yes, we've seen the cache TTL was accidentally set to 30s in a config change, that was my fault, fixed around 07:30 UTC on the 14th.

[02:25] Samir: Thanks for the transparency. On the cost side, if we right-size batching and pin a lighter model variant for the triage route you can shave off 25–35% of those marginal token costs. But the economics depend on committed capacity — we'll map that out.

[03:02] Nina: From procurement perspective, our finance team needs a deterministic uplift estimate: if we commit to 12 months, what's the expected monthly burn vs current pay-as-you-go?

[03:20] Samir: We can model that; Olivia will run a baseline benchmark with your top-3 prompts and we’ll simulate reserved throughput vs burst usage. We'll include a blended token/unit price.

[03:48] Olivia: Quick note on methodology — we'll run steady-state throughput at your current p50 latency target and a 24-hour spike window to simulate your end-of-month batch jobs. That gives p50/p95 and per-token billed cost.

[04:10] Rachel: That would help. Our main asks are: 1) keep user-facing latency under 300ms p95 for conversational flows, 2) cap cost increase at 15% over current monthly until we migrate the trimming logic, and 3) ensure audit logs for PII requests.

[04:33] Diego: We can commit to helping meet those: latency SLOs are often a combination of model selection, batching policy, and region routing. For audit logs we provide request/response hashing and persistent audit trails for Dedicated/Private.

[04:55] Evan: On region routing — we run across EU and us-east; do you have capacity in eu-west-1? We had some fallback routing to us-east which added 40ms.

[05:10] Olivia: Yes eu-west is available; looks like some requests routed to us-east due to ephemeral capacity constraints the week of July 12. If you opt for Dedicated reserved shards, routing stays local unless you set failover to cross-region.

[05:33] Priya: Ok good. Can we talk about VPC and key mgmt? Our legal requires KMS control and no egress to public buckets.

[05:44] Samir: Absolutely — Private deployments support customer-managed KMS keys and we have an on-prem option for air-gapped needs. For VPC peering we have a checklist; Connor will follow up with a support ticket.

[06:05] Nina: On the legal / procurement front I need SOC2 type II evidence and SLAs spelled out. Do you have a SOC2 package and uptime SLA samples?

[06:18] Diego: Yes we’ll share SOC2 artifacts under an NDA and provide sample SLA addenda. We usually do a security deep-dive with our security engineering team for enterprise commitments.

[06:33] Rachel: Great. From the platform team perspective, we care about graceful degradation — if Dedicated is saturated, what's the fallback model?

[06:45] Olivia: We recommend a two-tier model fallback: primary pinned model, then a quantized variant that keeps latency similar but lower token cost, and a last-resort smaller model for low importance requests. Routing policies can be configured per route. There's also auto-fallback for canary rollout failures.

[07:10] Evan: Did you see any errors or throttles in the 12–14 window? Our logs showed a few 429s but also some 5xx from our upstream service.

[07:23] Connor (Support): We flagged a handful of transient 429s tied to a routing flapping event. We correlate that with a control-plane heartbeat issue that coincided with the cache TTL flip Priya mentioned.\n
[07:38] Rachel: So in practice, if we commit, will those flapping events disappear?

[07:45] Samir: They should reduce significantly. Dedicated reserved shards remove cross-tenant scheduling contention. There can still be operational incidents, but your mean time to mitigate is typically faster because you own the capacity pool and we provide a priority support path.

[08:05] Priya: Good. About the benchmark — can you include measures for continuous batching efficiency and per-request cold-start? The cold-starts are what kill our p95.

[08:18] Olivia: We'll add a cold-start test matrix: short windows of sparse traffic vs sustained traffic and prefix cache warmup curves.

[08:32] Rachel: Also, can you show the impact of quantization? We rely on high-quality responses for clinical summarization; quantized models are fine if the ROUGE and hallucination metrics stay within a threshold.

[08:47] Olivia: We can run a small eval harness on your sample prompt set to compare generation quality across float32, int8-ish quantized variants, and a mid-sized pruned model. Expect tradeoffs: int8 often preserves fluency but may shift rare-token usage. We'll report BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics and a manual spot check.

[09:20] Nina: On procurement cadence, if the numbers look good and security signs off, we aim to approve a 12-month commitment in early September. Is that workable?

[09:32] Samir: Yes that's reasonable. Timeline-wise: Olivia's benchmark results by Aug 24, we send pricing and draft MSA by Aug 25, security deep-dive week of Aug 29, final decision early September.

[09:48] Evan: For the benchmarking env — do you need a VPC peering or can we provide a dataset and standalone API keys?

[09:58] Olivia: For pure latency/cost benchmarks, API keys suffice. For end-to-end network measurements and KMS flow we need a VPC test peering. We'll start with API-based bench and move to peered tests as a second step.

[10:20] Rachel: There's an operational ask: our SREs want the per-token cost exported to our internal billing daily so we can track anomalies in near real time.

[10:32] Diego: We have token-level billing export hooks and a daily usage CSV you can ingest. We can also send webhook-based anomaly alerts.

[10:45] Priya: Ok please enable the daily export for us.

[10:50] Connor: I'll set up the export and include the schema.

[11:05] Samir: Quick hit on numbers — for customers similar to you, a 12-month reserved footprint that covers 60–70% of steady-state shows 20–30% cost reduction vs PAYG, and combined with batching/pinning improvements you can target ~35% reduction on marginal token spend.

[11:32] Rachel: That 60–70% number — is that committed in slots or some throughput unit? Our CFO will ask specifics.

[11:40] Samir: We model as reserved QPS and memory-backed shards; we'll translate to an expected tokens-per-month commitment in the pricing spreadsheet.

[11:55] Nina: Legal will want termination terms and overage billing details.

[12:02] Samir: We'll include an example overage policy: soft cap notifications, then per-unit overage at a discounted PAYG rate. Termination terms are standard with a 30–60 day notice depending on the commercial tier.

[12:20] Evan: One more technical question — are model weights hosted in our account for Private deployments? We are concerned about data residency.

[12:30] Olivia: For Private on-prem, yes you host everything. For Private VPC we store model artifacts in our managed image registry but you can opt to mirror to a customer-controlled registry and control keys. We'll document the mirroring flow.

[12:50] Rachel: Roadmap items that matter to us: better autoscale policies (predictive), per-route canary configuration, longer audit log retention. Any ETA?

[13:03] Diego: Predictive autoscale is in beta; targeted GA in Q4. Per-route canaries and advanced rollouts are in our Q3 roadmap; audit retention is configurable via add-on currently. We'll share the roadmap snippet.

[13:28] Samir: I'll summarize what we promised and the immediate follow-ups. Olivia: benchmarks and cost sim. Connor: VPC checklist and billing export. Diego: SOC2 artifacts and roadmap snippet. Bluefield: confirm security reviewer and decision timeline.

[13:52] Rachel: Sounds good. A quick clarifying question on the bench: can you simulate the end-of-month spike pattern we saw in July where it's mostly triage threads hitting the models for ~45 minutes?

[14:05] Olivia: Yes we'll create a spike profile with ~3x baseline traffic for a 45m window and measure p95 and token cost.

[14:20] Nina: Procurement ask — will you provide a draft SOW and example invoice schedule with the pricing?

[14:28] Samir: Yes. We’ll include SOW and sample invoice cadence tied to committed units.

[14:40] Evan: Any caveats we should prepare for with Dedicated rollout — e.g., rolling updates causing brief capacity loss?

[14:50] Olivia: We do rolling upgrades with cross-shard draining; you can configure maintenance windows. For mission-critical workloads we recommend canary rollouts plus automatic fallback policies to avoid user-visible errors.

[15:08] Rachel: All right. If we get the benchmark and pricing and security evidence, we'll present to the execs and aim for internal approval by Sept 6.

[15:20] Samir: Perfect — that's aligned. Anything else?

[15:28] Priya: Small ask: can you provide a sample of the per-route latency dashboards we would get in Console?

[15:35] Diego: We'll send screenshots and a temporary demo tenant to explore dashboards.

[15:45] Nina: We'll expect the draft commercial by Aug 25.

[15:50] Samir: Great. Thank you everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.

[16:00] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings ("KV cash", "VPCe"), typical of automated transcriptions. The call included a mix of AE/SE/CSM-led items and ended with explicit next steps for procurement, benchmarks, and security review.
